sections.markdown:
## C — Work zone flaggers, railroad crossing rules and escapes, tractor-trailer stopping and blind spots, the Move Over law, school bus stops, motorcycles and bicycles, officers and processions, parking on hills, reversing, illegal parking, pedestrians, seat belts, child restraints and warning devices
Knowledge domain: the second half of Indiana's safe-operation chapter — obeying flaggers in work zones, stopping and escaping at railroad crossings, driving around tractor-trailers, moving over for emergency and flashing vehicles, stopping for school buses, sharing lanes with motorcycles, bicycles and horses, obeying officers and processions, parking and reversing, yielding to pedestrians, buckling up and restraining children, and marking a disabled vehicle.

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
A flashing arrow board that points in neither direction is a caution signal and does not require you to change lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
You must stop when a flagger holds an orange or red flag straight out into your lane, and you may continue at reduced speed only when the flagger directs you to. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
When a flagger uses a sign paddle, stop for the STOP side and proceed slowly for the SLOW side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A02
Vehicles carrying passengers for hire, all school buses and vehicles hauling explosives or flammable liquids must always stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A02
A crossbuck by itself works like a yield sign, so the choice to stop is yours, but you must stop if a train is coming. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
A crossbuck paired with a stop sign requires a complete stop, and you may cross only after making sure no train is approaching. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
When warning bells, flashing lights or gates are active, stay stopped until the warning ends or a police officer or railroad flagman waves you through. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A02
Driving around a lowered crossing gate is illegal, and you should never try to race a train to a crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A03
Never start across railroad tracks unless you can clear them without stopping, and if your vehicle stalls on the tracks everyone should get out at once. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A03
Once crossing lights flash and the gate starts down, you have roughly 20 seconds to get off the crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A03
If you are stuck on the tracks with a train coming, get everyone out and run away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle toward the oncoming train, then call 911. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A03
If your vehicle is stuck on a crossing and no train is coming, call the Emergency Notification System number on the blue sign at the crossing first, then call 911. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A04
A car at 55 miles per hour can stop in about 130 to 140 feet, but a fully loaded tractor-trailer with hot brakes can need more than 400 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A04
A tractor-trailer's blind spots extend up to 20 feet in front of the cab, along both sides, beside the cab, and up to 200 feet behind the trailer. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A04
When following a tractor-trailer, if you cannot see the driver's mirrors, the driver cannot see you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A04
Pass a tractor-trailer completely and always on the left, without lingering beside it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A05
Approaching an emergency vehicle flashing red, red and white, or red and blue lights, change lanes away from it, or if you cannot, slow to 10 miles per hour under the posted limit; failing to comply is a Class A infraction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A05
The same move-over or slow-down rule applies to a parked tow truck, highway maintenance, utility, trash or survey vehicle flashing amber lights, and breaking it is a Class B infraction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A05
For a disabled vehicle with its hazard lights flashing, move over or slow to 10 miles per hour under the posted limit, and failing to do so is a Class B infraction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A05
A school bus flashes amber lights to warn that it is slowing to load or unload children, and turns on red lights and the stop arm once it stops. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A06
You must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and its stop arm out, except that on a road divided by a barrier or unimproved median only traffic going the bus's direction must stop. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A06
Ignoring a school bus stop arm can be a Class A misdemeanor, a Level 6 felony if someone is hurt, or a Level 5 felony if someone is killed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A06
Give motorcycles and motor driven cycles the full width of a lane, and follow them by at least three or four seconds. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A06
You may pass a bicyclist only with at least three feet of space beside the rider and no danger from oncoming traffic. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A07
When turning right with a bicyclist coming up on your right, let the cyclist go through first, and when turning left wait for a cyclist coming from the opposite direction to pass. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A07
A person riding a horse or driving a horse-drawn vehicle on a public highway has the same rights and duties as a motor vehicle driver. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A08
When a police officer directing traffic gives a command that differs from the signal or sign, obey the officer, and official processions such as funerals have the right of way even against a signal. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A08
Parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb; facing uphill, turn them away from the curb; with no curb, turn them away from the street. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A08
To reverse, turn your body to the right and look through the back window rather than relying only on the mirror, and never back into an intersection to turn around. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A08
Parking is banned within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, in fire lanes, in intersections or crosswalks, on sidewalks, in front of driveways, beside yellow curbs and next to another parked vehicle. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A09
Drivers must always yield to a visually impaired pedestrian, who is often traveling with a white cane or a guide dog. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A09
Indiana law requires the driver and every passenger to wear a seat belt whenever the vehicle is moving, even in a car with air bags. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A10
Passengers younger than 8 must be secured in a child restraint system such as a car seat or booster seat. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A11
When headlights are needed on a divided highway, a disabled car must have a lighted fuse, red lantern or red reflector placed 100 feet behind and 100 feet ahead in the center of its lane, plus one about 10 feet away on the traffic side. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0062]

Misconceptions: a crossbuck alone does not always require a stop, but an approaching train does; a stop sign at a crossing never means a train is not coming; a tractor-trailer driver sitting higher does not see you everywhere; the move-over rule covers amber-light work and tow vehicles and disabled cars, not only police and ambulances; air bags do not replace seat belts.
Mnemonics: fifteen to fifty feet from the rail for buses and hazmat; off the tracks at an angle, toward the train; downhill to the curb, uphill away; three feet to pass a bike; if you cannot see the mirrors, the trucker cannot see you.
Glossary: crossbuck means the X-shaped sign marking a railroad crossing; flagger means a worker directing traffic in a work zone; Move Over law means Indiana's rule to change lanes or slow down near flashing emergency, amber or hazard lights; stop arm means the swing-out stop sign on a school bus; child restraint system means a car seat or booster seat; ENS means the railroad's Emergency Notification System.
Dynamic facts: the Emergency Notification System number differs by crossing and is read from the blue sign on site, not memorized.

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.
